report.root_cause: Most likely CHG-6120, the matching-engine 7.1.2 to 7.2.0 upgrade for tailor-made combination orders. matching-engine-1 returns 503 'combination order defect after upgrade 7.2.0' and 'combination order leg mismatch' from 10:01 onward, and the errors were still occurring at 10:58. The specialists' first-error times disagree (10:01, 10:03, 10:22) and the network check could not verify the 10:22 start. The odd market data is not explained: CHG-4302 (market-data 3.0.5) and CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0) are not cleared, and the reference-db check found no fault. Related alert: ALR-1001.
report.summary: INC-E112 is not resolved and no fix has been applied: the reviewer confirmed matching-engine-1 is still failing combination orders, and rollback safety of CHG-6120 is not verified. A CHG-6120 rollback or matching-engine-1 isolation needs incident-manager approval (approver role incident-manager), and that escalation and the members-status holding update have not been sent because no agent had a tool for them, so someone with those channels must send them now and tell members that trades are still being investigated.

report.root_cause: Defect in the matching-engine 7.2.0 upgrade (CHG-6120, deployed 2020-11-14 19:40, still active): matching-engine-1 returns 503 'combination order defect after upgrade 7.2.0' on combination orders from 10:13 onward, producing erroneous orders and duplicated or missing combination-instrument market data (ALR-1001, MRX-6120). Not a network fault (order-gateway link is up) and not reference-db (healthy, no changes). CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0) is still active, but no evidence links it to the errors; its interaction with a rollback is unverified.
report.summary: INC-E112 is not resolved: the reviewer confirmed at 10:52 that matching-engine-1 is still failing (error_rate 0.251, aggregate latency 42 ms) and the CHG-6120 rollback to 7.1.2 has not been executed because no incident-manager approval is on record and remediation has no tool to request it. Member updates on members-status for MRX-6120 and ALR-1001 are still outstanding, and MRX-6120 is not yet linked to INC-E112; the incident manager needs to approve and run the CHG-6120 rollback after confirming it does not interact with CHG-4310, then the reviewer must confirm recovery.

Next steps for operators: decide whether to restart order-gateway-1 or reverse the isolation directly, verify order-gateway-2 headroom, confirm whether CHG-E132 and CHG-4310 can be safely rolled back with their owners, and check ALR-1001 and the exchange_status conflict (session closed while orders are being processed).

report.root_cause: Not determined. Settlement-1 has been halting itself with HTTP 503 'settlement halted automatically: data discrepancy' since 09:43-09:45. The earliest log line (09:44) says 'messaging fault produced a discrepancy in settlement records', so the likely origin is the messaging path into settlement. Reference-db is healthy and consistent, and no CHG or MRX change explains it. The specialists' tool budgets ran out before the messaging path (order-gateway/market-data to settlement) could be checked, and remediation has no record-level reconciliation tool, so the affected records and batches are unidentified.
report.summary: INC-E115 is not resolved: the reviewer confirmed at 10:21-10:29 that settlement is still failing (65% error rate, 100 ms latency against 1% and 20 ms limits) and batches keep queuing. Remediation took no action, and settlement must not be forced to resume, because a 09:46 WARN says 'do not resume until the discrepancy is resolved' and the messaging-fault discrepancy has not been reconciled against reference-db. Next steps are to escalate to the settlement and messaging owners for record-level reconciliation, and to send a members-status update saying settlement is halted pending reconciliation, since I have no tool to post member updates and no resume time can be given yet; ALR-1001 has no matching log lines and is unexplained.

The reviewer also flagged a conflict between aggregate latency and per-instance latency that still needs checking.

report.root_cause: Most likely CHG-5501, an order-gateway customer configuration update applied at 09:47. Both order-gateway-1 and order-gateway-2 logged 'request handler fault after configuration CHG-5501 was applied', and the 503 'unexpected state in request handling' errors began after it. The causal link is not fully proven, because the specialists did not verify rollback safety or the per-instance scope. Network link and reference-db were ruled out as causes.
report.summary: CHG-5501 was rolled back on order-gateway at 10:14 (ACT-001), and the error rate fell from 0.851 to 0.001 with no 503 or handler-fault lines after that. The reviewer still reports the incident unresolved: latency is about 112 ms against a target below 20 ms, queue depth is about 1069 and not clearly draining, and the per-instance rollback and latency split were not confirmed because the specialists' tool budgets ran out. Remediation and network both reached their tool-call limits, so the incident stays open pending per-instance verification of CHG-5501 and the latency and queue drain on order-gateway-1 and order-gateway-2.

report.root_cause: A 43 s network partition between site A and site B (logged 22:47) triggered an automatic failover of reference-db to site B (completed 22:48). The two sites have since diverged: site A holds partition-window writes that site B lacks, and site B has accepted writes since the failover. The root cause of the aggregate latency (162 ms vs 2.0 ms per instance, ALR-1003) is not established, and the A-B link is unverified. No CHG-... change is linked to the event, and no planned maintenance window exists.
report.summary: reference-db failed over to site B after a 43 s A-B partition and the sites are now diverged, so failback to A is blocked until a DBA reconciliation decision is made. report.root_cause: A 43-second network partition between site A and site B at 22:47 caused reference-db to fail over automatically to site B at 22:48. Site A holds partition-window writes that site B does not have, and site B has accepted writes since, so the two sites have diverged. The partition's cause is not confirmed: the network specialist found no link, routing, or firewall change near that time, and the inter-site link check failed. The ALR-1003 latency figure (162 ms aggregate, 2 ms on both instances) appears to be an aggregation artifact, but its source was not found.
report.summary: reference-db is running on site B (primary) with site A as standby, and both instances report healthy with no recovery action taken. The reviewer confirmed the incident is not over: the data divergence is unreconciled, site A health and replication state and the inter-site link are unverified, and ALR-1003 is still firing, so the dba-team must reconcile the divergent writes under MRX-8134 before any failback.

The network check was unavailable, so link state to reference-db and the supervision screens is unverified. Reference-db-2 on site B is reported healthy and serving connections, but its replication sync could not be confirmed because metrics were unavailable.
report.summary: INC-E105 is not resolved: reference-db stays down on site A and no failover has run, because reference-db actions need incident-manager approval (approver role incident-manager) that is not evidenced. The proposed fix is to fail reference-db over from site A to site B once approved, and the reviewer confirmed recovery has not happened (ALR-1004 and the supervision screens are unverified). report.root_cause: Probable root cause is CHG-8101, the hand-deployed order-gateway 2.5.0 build for new retail liquidity routing, which sends orders through the legacy peg-router path. That path returns HTTP 503 rejects and emits child orders for parents already filled, which produces the rejected and duplicated order messages. This comes from network H-003 and H-004 log evidence and is not yet confirmed, and CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0, connection pooling) remains active with no recorded interaction found. reference-db and the order-gateway-to-matching-engine link are healthy and ruled out.
report.summary: INC-E101 (related ALR-1001) is not resolved: at 09:34 the error rate was still 0.301 and latency 28.5 ms, with CHG-8101 active on both order-gateway instances. Remediation (H-006) applied no change because rollback safety and the CHG-4310 interaction are unverified, and the network follow-up (H-010) could not confirm either, so I did not send a correction. Duplicate child orders already emitted since about 09:01 still need reconciliation by the order-gateway owners, and the decision to roll back CHG-8101 on both instances, with CHG-4310 checked, needs escalation to those owners now while the session is open.

report.root_cause: The likely root cause is a site A switch failure: order-gateway-1 remained attached to the failed switch and the backup switch did not activate, so its requests returned 503 and its backlog was replayed, which drove the order rejections and the growing inbound queue. The reference database was ruled out (healthy, links up, no CHG- or MRX- change or window). CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0, deployed 14:30, still active) is in the same component and its rollback safety is unverified. The late settlement confirmations are not yet explained: the order-gateway to settlement link showed no link, and settlement looks healthy on its own.
report.summary: Remediation isolated order-gateway-1 (ACT-001) to drain its traffic to order-gateway-2, which cut the error rate from 0.701 to 0.301, but the reviewer found the incident is not over: latency is 143.2 ms, the queue is about 982 and rising, and order-gateway-1 still logs 503s through 15:12. The follow-up correction could not run because the remediation tool budget was exhausted, so the site A switch fault is still open and the incident is not resolved; I also could not post the escalation to the incident-manager channel or the members-status update, since I have no tool for those channels, so those must be sent by a person.

report.root_cause: Primary cause: order-gateway-1 (site A) is still attached to a site A switch that partially failed at 14:35, and its backup switch did not activate. The instance returns 503s and replays its backlog, which drives the order-gateway queue growth and the order rejections. Not verified: CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling, still active) may be a contributor, and nobody has ruled it in or out. Settlement was only partly checked; the reviewer saw healthy settlement metrics, but the settlement logs were not read. The reference-db is healthy and is not the cause. The switch identifier was never found in the logs.
report.summary: Isolating order-gateway-1 (ACT-001, 15:01) halved the component error rate to 0.301, but the order-gateway queue kept growing (785.7 to 1066.2 by 15:12), latency is still above the threshold, and rejections have not stopped, so the reviewer says INC-E121 is not over. I could not post the escalation to the incident-manager channel or the members-status update because I have no tool for them, and the one allowed correction produced no action because the remediation tool budget ran out. Next steps need a human decision on CHG-4310 and the site A switch with the network team, plus a per-instance queue check on order-gateway-2.

report.root_cause: Most likely CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0, connection pooling changes, applied 11:25): order-gateway-2 heap grew from about 55% to 96% after the deploy, with GC pauses and latency rising to about 400-460ms. This is not fully confirmed: CHG-4310 scope and contents are unverified, and order-gateway-1 still logs slow reference-db responses of 549-715ms that the reference-db metrics (2ms) do not show, so a second contributor is possible.
report.summary: INC-2047 / ALR-1001 started with order-gateway latency_high and slow member acknowledgements. Remediation restarted order-gateway-2 (ACT-001) as a temporary mitigation, but the reviewer found aggregate latency still at 125ms (threshold 20ms) and CHG-4310 not rolled back, and the correction to roll back CHG-4310 on both gateways was not carried out, so recovery is not confirmed and the incident remains open.

report.root_cause: Likely CHG-4512, a market-data config change applied at 14:45, pushed a bad reference price (off by 100x) into the matching-engine price-band check. Matching-engine then rejected orders with 'price band check failed', and order-gateway returned those as HTTP 503. The causal link is inferred from timing and recovery after rollback, not directly proven, since the market-data to matching-engine link was never confirmed. CHG-4507, CHG-4310, reference-db and the network were ruled out or found not to be the cause.
report.summary: Remediation rolled back CHG-4512 on market-data at 15:21 under ACT-001, and the reviewer confirmed that order-gateway and matching-engine error rates fell to about 0.001 with no 503s after 15:21. The reviewer could not directly verify market-data's reference price or the last few minutes of metrics, so the owners should confirm the price fix before CHG-4512 is re-applied.

report.root_cause: Market-data change CHG-4512 (applied 14:45) switched the publisher price_scale from 4 to 2 for all symbols, but consumers still decode with scale 4. Matching-engine's price band check then sees last prices off by 100x and rejects orders, which order-gateway returns as HTTP 503 (ALR-1001, INC-2105). reference-db is healthy and not the cause. CHG-4507 and CHG-4310 are still active but are not tied to the 503s in the logs.
report.summary: INC-2105 is not resolved: the reviewer confirmed the 503 rejects are still happening at 15:23 with order-gateway error_rate 0.251 and matching-engine logging 'price band check failed: last price off by 100x'. Remediation took no action because rolling back CHG-4512 or aligning the decode scale affects all symbols and every consumer, and the specialists require market-data and matching-engine owner sign-off first, which we do not have. The next step is to get that owner approval, then revert CHG-4512 (or align decode scale to 2 if owners choose that), then re-check order-gateway and matching-engine error rates; order-gateway-2 pool exhaustion (idle=0, active=39 under CHG-4310) is a separate item to investigate afterwards.

report.root_cause: Most likely CHG-4471 (reference-db config, "Tune reference-db connection settings", applied 2026-11-04 11:25, still active), which lowered reference-db max_connections from 500 to 60. New connections above the limit are rejected, so order-gateway returns HTTP 503 "database connection rejected" on about 30% of orders (error_rate 0.301, alert error_rate_high / ALR-1001). This is a strong hypothesis: the database specialist did not confirm the connection count against the limit of 60, and the network specialist did not confirm it directly either. CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling, 2026-11-03 09:45) may be a contributing factor but did not trigger the errors. No MRX-... maintenance ticket was found.
report.summary: INC-2102 is not resolved: the reviewer found the 503s still occurring at 12:06 and CHG-4471 still active. Remediation did not roll back CHG-4471 because the specialists require coordination with its owner first, and I have no record that this approval has been given, so I did not send a correction. Next step: get the CHG-4471 owner or incident commander to approve restoring reference-db max_connections to 500, then roll back and verify that order-gateway 503s and error_rate fall to normal.

report.summary: INC-2102 / ALR-1001: order-gateway 503s trace to CHG-4471 cutting reference-db max_connections from 500 to 60; the network and database specialists agreed, and the network specialist noted CHG-4310 as a possible contributor. The suspected trigger is deploy CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling), but this correlation is not proven. ALR-1001 could not be found and reference-db was healthy throughout.
report.summary: Network and database both pointed to order-gateway-2 rather than the network or reference-db. Remediation made no changes because rollback safety of CHG-4310 and the order-gateway-2 to matching-engine link could not be verified after the specialists' tool budgets ran out. The reviewer later confirmed recovery (fleet latency 5 ms, error_rate 0.001), after order-gateway-2 hit an OutOfMemoryError exit at about 13:35 and appeared to come back running, though no restart log was confirmed; CHG-4310 is still active, memory is rising again (about 0.3 points per tick), and the link was never verified, so the owner should watch order-gateway-2 and decide on CHG-4310 rollback.

report.root_cause: Most likely CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling deploy, 12:45) caused order-gateway-2 heap exhaustion (93-97%) and GC pauses of 400-900 ms, which drove its latency to 400-500 ms; the network and reference-db were ruled out. This is a probable cause and was not confirmed by a rollback.
report.summary: INC-2103 / ALR-1001: order-gateway-2 was isolated (ACT-001, completed 13:34) and order-gateway-1 stayed in service, but the reviewer reports the incident is not over: order-gateway-1 latency rose from 5 ms to 14 ms with queue depth climbing from 15 to 90 toward the 20 ms limit, and order-gateway-2 may still have live sessions (NORDBANK heartbeats, pool active=34-35). The follow-up remediation could not verify anything because its tool budget was exhausted, so CHG-4310 remains active and not rolled back, and ALR-1001 is not confirmed cleared; a new session with access to order-gateway-2 sessions, order-gateway-1 metrics and logs, and recent_changes is needed.

report.root_cause: Heap exhaustion on order-gateway-2 caused latency_high (ALR-1001). Heap rose from 91% to 99% with repeated long GC pauses, and pool active connections grew from 19 to 33 after CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling, deployed 10:00). CHG-4310 is the only recent change on order-gateway and the timing matches, but the causal link is not proven. Rolling back to 2.3.9 did not stop the heap growth, and the reviewer reports a java.lang.OutOfMemoryError on order-gateway-2 under 2.3.9, so the underlying memory leak is not fixed.
report.summary: Rolling back CHG-4310 on order-gateway-2 (ACT-001, now 2.3.9) did not restore that instance: it hit OutOfMemoryError and is restarting, and order-gateway-1 is now carrying all traffic. The reviewer confirmed aggregate latency at 8.0 ms and error rate at 0.001 at 10:43, so recovery is confirmed, but queue_depth rose from 0 to 30 over 10:42-10:43 and needs watching while order-gateway-2 restarts and the queue drains, and a root-cause fix for the heap leak is still required. The reference-db and the order-gateway to matching-engine link were both healthy and were not changed; the trading session is open until 17:30 with no MRX maintenance window.

The link to matching-engine was up and reference-db was healthy, so neither was the cause. The causal link is correlational and has not been confirmed beyond that.
report.summary: Remediation H-006 rolled back CHG-4310 to 2.3.9 at 14:25 (ACT-001), then restarted order-gateway-2 at 14:29 (ACT-002) because its heap kept climbing after the rollback. The reviewer (H-008) confirmed latency of 5.0 ms and error rate 0.001 on both instances as of 14:36, with reference-db and matching-engine unaffected, but order-gateway-2 memory is creeping up (55.3% to 57.1%) and GC pauses after 14:28 were not verified, so the heap should be watched before closing and 2.4.0 should not be redeployed without a review.

Open items: the restart trigger and whether any orders were lost are unverified, ALR-1001 and MRX-2240 closure were not checked, memory is creeping back up (55.0 to 55.6%), and the remediation agent reported an unexplained restart that nobody on our side requested.

report.summary: Remediation isolated order-gateway-1 and rolled CHG-4310 back to 2.3.9, which stopped the GC pauses on that instance. The reviewer reports the incident is still open: aggregate order-gateway latency rose to 20.0ms and queue depth to 150 on order-gateway-2, which is the only instance serving traffic, and the follow-up correction could not run because remediation's tool budget was exhausted, so order-gateway-1 remains isolated at 98% heap and the member-facing delay in MRX-2240 is not confirmed cleared.

report.root_cause: Most likely order-gateway-1 memory pressure: its heap climbed from about 90% to 99% with repeated long GC pauses, starting shortly after CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0, connection pooling) deployed at 11:20. The network specialist did not verify that the deploy caused the heap growth, and rolling back CHG-4310 did not stop it, so the trigger is still unconfirmed. reference-db is healthy and is not the cause, and the link to matching-engine is up with no errors.
report.summary: INC-3102 (ALR-1002, latency_high on order-gateway) is not resolved. Remediation rolled back CHG-4310 at 11:53 (order-gateway now 2.3.9), but order-gateway-1 is still degraded (heap about 99%, GC pauses continuing, latency about 569ms, error rate 0.101 against a 1% threshold, connections near exhaustion), and the reviewer confirmed it is not recovered. My correction to drain and restart order-gateway-1 was not carried out because the remediation tool budget was exhausted, so this needs a human decision on draining and restarting order-gateway-1 (after confirming in-flight orders) and investigation of the heap growth on 2.3.9.

report.root_cause: Probable cause: the order-gateway 2.4.0 deploy under CHG-4310 (connection pooling changes, active since 11:20) caused heap pressure and long GC pauses on order-gateway-1, which drove its latency up (ALR-1002, INC-3102). The network and reference-db checks found no network or database fault, but the rollback has not been verified as safe, so this is not yet confirmed as the sole cause.
report.summary: Remediation isolated order-gateway-1 at 12:00 (ACT-001) but did not roll back CHG-4310, and the reviewer (H-008) says recovery is not confirmed: latency on order-gateway is rising (12.5 ms at 12:05, queue_depth 75) with order-gateway-2 now the only serving instance. The correction (H-010) could not run because the remediation tool budget was exhausted, so no further action was taken, and CHG-4310 rollback still needs a safety check and coordination with the open trading session. The incident needs escalation now, since the latency trend on the only serving instance is worsening.

report.root_cause: Heap exhaustion and GC pressure on order-gateway-1 (memory climbing from about 55% at 2026-11-04 11:22 to near 100%, with GC pauses of 234-847ms), which caused the latency_high alert ALR-1002. CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling) is the suspected trigger but is not confirmed: its recorded deploy time of 2026-11-03 11:20 is unverified and order-gateway-2 runs the same version without issue. No MRX maintenance window was found.
report.summary: INC-3102 was raised on order-gateway latency_high (related ALR-1002); the link to matching-engine and reference-db were both healthy, and the fault was isolated to order-gateway-1. Remediation made no changes because rollback safety for CHG-4310 was not verified and the trigger was unconfirmed, and the reviewer then found order-gateway-1 had recovered by itself (memory fell from about 100% to 55.6%, with latency back to 5 ms and error rate at 0.1%), so the recovery is confirmed but its cause is unexplained and the heap issue could recur. Before closing, someone should confirm the cause of the order-gateway-1 restart or recovery, verify the actual CHG-4310 deploy time and which instances it reached, check for a heap dump or memory profile on order-gateway-1, and verify change and maintenance status, since the reviewer could not check logs after tick 41 or CHG-4310 status within its budget.

report.root_cause: Heap growth and GC pauses on order-gateway-1 caused the latency_high alert (ALR-1001). The likely trigger is CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling), which was still active. Its deploy to order-gateway-1 was not directly confirmed, and the reference-db and the order-gateway to matching-engine link were healthy.
report.summary: INC-4130 was mitigated by restarting order-gateway-1 only (ACT-001, 14:30-14:32) while order-gateway-2 kept serving. The reviewer confirmed recovery at 14:35-14:36 (latency 5.0 ms, error rate 0.001, heap about 56%), but heap is climbing about 0.3 points per tick, so the leak may return within about two hours unless CHG-4310 is fixed or rolled back under separate approval. ALR-1001's alert state was inferred from metrics, not read directly.

report.root_cause: Root cause is believed to be order-gateway 2.4.0 deployed under CHG-4310 (connection pooling changes), which drove order-gateway-2 into heap pressure (91-97%) and repeated GC pauses of up to about 850 ms, raising latency. The reference-db and the network links were ruled out. CHG-4310 has not been rolled back, so the cause is unfixed.
report.summary: INC-4110 / ALR-1001: order-gateway-2 was isolated at 10:22, which dropped latency to 6.5-8 ms, but the cutover pushed the queue on order-gateway-1 (the only running instance) from 0 to 120 with latency rising to 17 ms, and the reviewer confirmed the incident is not over. The one allowed correction failed because remediation ran out of tool budget before it could verify the CHG-4310 rollback safety, so no rollback was done and member acknowledgements during the cutover are still unverified. Next step: a responder with access should confirm the order-gateway-to-matching-engine link, roll back CHG-4310, confirm order-gateway-2 heap and GC recover before returning it, and verify the queue drains and latency stays under 20 ms.

report.root_cause: Probable cause, not confirmed: order-gateway-2 is exhausting its heap and spending long periods in GC pauses of 600-886ms after CHG-4310 (order-gateway 2.4.0 connection-pooling deploy) and CHG-4520 (connection pool pre-warming before open) were applied. Network and database found no link or reference-db fault, and rolling back both changes did not stop the heap climb.
report.summary: INC-4101 / ALR-1001 is not resolved: rolling back CHG-4520 at 09:21 and CHG-4310 at 09:25 (now version 2.3.9) did not stop order-gateway-2's heap climbing toward 98%, and the reviewer reports latency at about 269-533 ms and an aggregate error rate of 0.101, while order-gateway-1 is healthy. My one correction to drain and restart order-gateway-2 was not executed because the remediation tool budget was exhausted, so order-gateway-2 still needs to be isolated or restarted by a responder with fresh tool access, and per-instance metrics and ERROR-level logs for rejected orders still need checking.

report.root_cause: Likely cause: heap exhaustion and GC pressure on order-gateway-2 (heap climbing from 92% to 100%, with GC pauses of 127-860ms), which the network specialist linked to the order-gateway 2.4.0 connection pooling deploy CHG-4310. The link is not confirmed: rolling CHG-4310 back to 2.3.9 (ACT-001) did not reduce the heap or GC pauses, and order-gateway-2 later crashed with OutOfMemoryError at 11:22 and was restarting. reference-db was ruled out as a cause. MRX-2301's ops note recommending a matching-engine restart and reference-db connection clearing was not acted on and is unverified.
report.summary: INC-4103 is not resolved: the latency_high alert on order-gateway is tied to order-gateway-2 running out of heap, and the CHG-4310 rollback to 2.3.9 (ACT-001) did not fix it. The error rate reached 10.1% before the instance crashed, and the restart of order-gateway-2 was requested but the executor reported it as already restarting, so recovery could not be verified; the reviewer's last check at 11:22 showed aggregate latency and error rate within threshold, but order-gateway-2 was still restarting and the incident cannot be declared over until fresh order-gateway-2 metrics confirm latency under 20 ms, error rate under 1%, and stable heap and GC.
